thread:
maria: heads up — we've been seeing a recurring tail latency spike on ephem NVMe in ap-southeast1 that lines up with preemptible GPU alloc failures this morning. example traces show long fsync waits, 200–600ms per fsync.

kai: copying logs, can you paste the sampler metrics?

maria: gist of the kibana query: `service:ephemeral-cleaner AND region:ap-southeast1 AND fsync_ms:[200 TO *]`

sam: that's the same window I saw. alloc controller retries then gives up (3 retries) and marks node unhealthy, so BG evict + restart.

elaine: /who is running scrub concurrently with batch jobs in that region?

maria: scrub cron at 03:10 UTC, batch window is 03:05–03:25 UTC for a bunch of preemptible launches. overlap is bad.

sam: quick snapshot from node gnode-54: `iostat -x 1 3` shows avg await 120ms, util 95% on nvme0n1 during the spike.

kai: suspect resource contention + aggressive fsync patterns from our janitor. ops-runner, any recent scrub tuning?

ops-runner: pushed scrub sampler concurrency bump to 16 -> 32 last week to reduce backlog on older drives. rollout targeted us-west but ap-southeast rolled later in the canary.

maria: looks like the ap-southeast hosts still had a high wear profile; increasing concurrency there -> oscillation under load.

elaine: can we throttle scrub concurrency per-zone based on SMART wear and current queue_depth? probably set default 8 for high-wear devices.

sam: agree. also we should change alloc controller fallback: treat preemptible requests as lower priority and route to eu-west if latency spike detected instead of immediate failure. that avoids mass failed starts.

kai: quick mitigation plan: 1) scale down scrub concurrency in ap-southeast1 to 8, 2) temporary increase batch start window jitter to spread launches, 3) add alloc fallback route to eu-west2 for preemptible. anyone object?

elaine: +1. how long to roll scrub throttle?

ops-runner: can flip a flag in the janitor config; rolling to ap-southeast1 should take ~6 min to reach all pods. I'll do a canary on one subnet first.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: janitor-config v2026.03.21-12 -> ap-southeast1-canary (1 pod)

maria: also add a temporary autoscale cushion: reserve an extra 10% dedicated capacity for 2 hours to absorb failed preemptible requests while we stabilize. cost hit small compared to failed launches.

sam: how do we measure success? metrics to watch: nvme_avg_await_ms, fsync_p99, preemptible_alloc_fail_rate, gpu_queue_delay.

kai: set alert thresholds: nvme_avg_await_ms > 150ms for 5m -> paging; preemptible_alloc_fail_rate > 1% over baseline -> alert.

ops-runner: canary config flipped -> concurrency=8 on subnet-a1. monitoring now.

maria: initial canary shows fsync p99 drop from 420ms -> 110ms on that subnet. good sign.

elaine: rolling to rest of ap-southeast now?

ops-runner: rolling in 3 batches, will pause if any node-level SMART reboots or if util drops below 70% (we don't want to underutilize).

sam: started re-routing preemptible allocations to eu-west2 for next 30m window.

infra-bot: route policy applied: preemptible_fallback -> eu-west2 for 30m

maria: update: after first batch roll (10 nodes), overall preemptible_alloc_failures dropped 78%, fsync_p99 region-wide down 60%.

elaine: nice. follow-ups: - add zone-aware scrub concurrency defaults, - implement wear-based dynamic throttle, - add start-window jitter by default for preemptible launches.

kai: and add an automatic alloc-fallback policy that triggers when fsync_p99 > 200ms for 2m.

ops-runner: filing follow-up ticket and will attach logs/graphs. ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/INFRA-3247

maria: thanks team. I'll monitor for the next 2h before we revert the temporary dedicated cushion.

sam: small note: we should also check firmware version skew — older firmware + heavy concurrent scrubs can spike write amplification. I'll run a scan.

ops-runner: scan kickstarted across ap-southeast fleet, results ETA 45m.

maria: if scan shows older firmware on majority, we'll schedule a non-disruptive firmware update wave next maintenance window.

elaine: thanks all. great quick ops. :tada:

kai: one-liner for postmortem: overlap of aggressive scrub concurrency with preemptible batch window led to fsync tail latency causing alloc failures; mitigated by throttling scrub, routing fallbacks, and temporary capacity cushion.

infra-bot: thread archived to infra-ops-archives after 2h of inactivity.
